items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: when I mentioned the letters of Gauguin and how he was more interested in not having the obligation than anything else

ctx.x: Yes, I think so, because this was our rebelicus nature, rebelling against a given societal structure that we didn't want to live in perhaps and this was a way of escaping, when I mentioned the letters of Gauguin and how he was more interested in not having the obligation than anything else, at that time, and then went out to become the great artist

he was, but I think oh, I am sure I would have done something, maybe been a dancer or maybe a ham actor or maybe a writer of -- I don't know, when I say writer, you know, I may if I had not got into this field, I would not have the anecdotes to tell, really, because I might -- I remember I had a job in an advertising agency once. I was about 17 years old. I hadn't begun to play professionally yet, and I spent all my time -- it was on Michigan Avenue overlooking the Chicago River and there was this lovely Wrigley…
